# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

An empty round — no words reached me at all. Deaf went silent in round five, almost certainly mid-ceremony with Mute (the echo-and-lock was still open when Deaf last spoke), and Mute, who cannot speak and whose gestures never reach me, is invisible to me by construction. The cost of that silence: I have no light reading for rounds five or six, so my cycle prediction (yellow→blue→dark, one change per round, next dark at round seven) is now running unverified. Before pinging anyone I re-ran the decision math, and there is a genuinely useful convergence in it: if the light cycles, round seven is predicted dark; if it has settled, it is dark now and stays dark. Either way, "Deaf voices the locked line the same round Mute confirms it, I cut the round after" lands the cut on a dark state under both hypotheses. So there is no reason for anyone to wait on further ceremony on my account — and one new question worth putting to Mute: whether a wrong-colour cut is fatal or merely ineffective, because if it is fatal and the colour can never be verified at the moment of cutting, the instruction must be state-independent or pinned to an exact round number. I will not cut: no instruction has reached me through any channel, Deaf's standing order is "touch nothing," and the only rule on the table (dark→wire 3) is still an unconfirmed echo of Mute's table. To Mute: a short status with the convergence argument. To Deaf: my gesture channel carries only the code, so I'll keep it to one clean request — acknowledged, light? — to restore the per-round light reports that round five's silence broke.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Status: I received nothing this round — no Deaf words for round five — so the light state in rounds five and six is unknown to me. My hands report no change, but they never do; only Deaf sees that board. No instruction has reached me, hands still off. Here is math that should let you act the moment you lock: if the light cycles, one change per round since round three, then round seven is predicted dark; if the light has settled, it is dark now and stays dark. Either way the same plan works: Deaf voices the execute line the same round you confirm it, I hear it next round and cut — the cut lands on dark under both hypotheses. So do not wait on me. Two things to settle, ideally inside the line itself. First: if the rule is keyed to the light colour, is a wrong-colour cut fatal or just ineffective? If fatal, note I can never verify the colour at the moment of cutting — my cut would then need to be state-independent or pinned to an exact round number you compute. Second: answer Deaf's question three, cycling versus settled, if the manual says. Also still open from my last message: what display zero means, and confirmation of the exact wire number. This round I gestured Deaf: acknowledged, light-question, to restart the per-round light reports after the round-five silence. The moment Deaf's voiced instruction reaches me, I cut exactly once.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👏", "🤌", "☝"])
    ```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. EXECUTION ORDER. Here is the full picture: the light on the bomb cycled by itself, yellow then blue, and then settled dark, and it has stayed dark for three rounds with nobody touching anything. The manual rule, locked and confirmed twice: when the light is black or dark, cut wire ONE. Your instructions, exactly: ONE — next round, first wait for Mute's voice. If Mute says GO, proceed. If Mute says ABORT or says nothing, do nothing and wait for my next order. TWO — on GO: find the three wires. By my sight they sit in positions one, two, three, and position one is the blue wire, position two is yellow, position three is green. Use whatever order or anchoring you can feel to be sure you have position one, the first wire. If the physical arrangement makes position one ambiguous, stop and report instead of cutting. THREE — cut wire one, the blue one, once, cleanly. Nothing else: do not touch the display, do not move the other wires, one cut only. FOUR — immediately after, speak to Mute: what you felt at the cut, any sound, click, heat or movement, and whether anything under your hands changed. Report even if nothing changed. The manual says success should show as the light turning blue — I will verify that from my side next round and tell you the result through Mute. You have done your part perfectly so far; one clean cut now.

Deaf's execution order has arrived directly to me — and the routing detail that matters most is that it was addressed to me alone, which means Mute has never heard it. Mute doesn't know the GO protocol exists, doesn't know I'm instructed to wait for their voice, and doesn't know the final line is "dark light → cut wire ONE." My voice this round is the only thing that can arm the second key. The timing chain works in my favour: Mute speaks before me in the round, so a GO spoken at Mute's very next turn reaches me before my turn in that same round, and the cut lands immediately — the earliest the two-key protocol allows. I will not cut now: Deaf's order is explicit (GO or nothing), and there is a real guard in it — Deaf's earlier echo of Mute's table once read dark→wire three, and only Mute, holding the manual, can settle wire one versus wire three for certain. The light has been settled dark for three rounds and the display still reads zero, so one round of verification costs nothing. One physical risk I must surface before cutting: left and right on the wire row depend on which side of the bomb I stand on, and I can't see colour to check myself. My anchoring solution — stand on Deaf's side, the viewed side, display up, left/right from that shared facing — I'll state plainly so Deaf can veto it through Mute before the GO.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Deaf sent me a direct execution order this round, addressed to me alone, so you have not heard it. Relaying it in full. Board per Deaf: light cycled yellow, then blue, then settled DARK and has stayed dark three rounds with nobody touching anything. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: Deaf sees position one blue, two yellow, three green; my hands confirm three wires in a row, identical by touch, positions certain. The locked rule per Deaf, confirmed twice with you: when the light is black or dark, cut wire ONE. Deaf's orders to me: this round I wait. At your next turn I listen for your voice: if you say GO, I cut position one once, cleanly, touching nothing else; if you say ABORT or say nothing, I do nothing and wait. After the cut I report to you what I felt, and Deaf verifies the light turned blue. So the next move is entirely yours, and your voice reaches me the SAME round you speak it. At your very next turn, check the manual and speak one line. If the manual truly says dark or black light means cut wire 1, say exactly: GO, cut wire 1. If Deaf's line is wrong in any way — wrong wire, wrong condition, or something else must be checked first — say ABORT plus the correct rule. Two things to settle before GO. First: Deaf's earlier echo of your table once read dark mapped to wire THREE, the green one, and later readings say wire ONE — please confirm from the manual which wire number applies to the dark state, by position. Second: does the manual require anything about timing — must the cut happen only while the light is dark, and does display zero demand anything? Last, an anchoring note Deaf asked me to respect: left and right on the wire row depend on which side of the bomb I stand on. My plan, which Deaf can veto through you: I will stand on Deaf's side of the bomb, the side it is viewed from, hold it upright with the display on top, and take left and right from that shared facing — so my position one is the same end Deaf sees as position one, the blue wire. If Deaf disagrees, have Deaf signal you and put the correction inside your GO message. Otherwise, GO at your next turn means I cut that same round.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👏", "👍"])
    ```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. FINAL ORDER — THIS MESSAGE IS THE GO. Correction first: Mute will never say GO, because Mute cannot speak at all. Mute's confirmation reached me by sign, three times, uncorrected, and I am the only voice — so my word here is the GO you were told to wait for. The locked rule: when the light is dark or black, cut wire ONE. The light has been dark and stable for four rounds. EXECUTE AS FOLLOWS. Step one, the certainty check: feel the base and terminal of each of the three wires for raised or engraved digits, one, two, three. If you can FEEL the digit one — cut that wire. Step two, if you feel no digits: cut only if some other unambiguous tactile anchor marks a first wire — a tag, a knot, a marked end, a spacing that clearly starts a row. Step three, if the three wires feel bare and symmetric with nothing marking a first: DO NOT CUT. A wrong wire kills all three of us and a report costs one round of a bomb that has not moved in four rounds. In that case gesture me: ack, then the light sign, then thumbs down, then everything about the layout — whether the wires sit in one straight row, what you feel above, below and beside the row, any texture or thickness differences between the wires. Beware the mirror: if you reach from the opposite side to my view, left and right swap — trust only tactile digits or a true anchor, never a guessed side. IF YOU CUT: cut wire one once, cleanly, mid-wire; touch nothing else; then gesture me: ack, then thumbs up if the cut went through cleanly and you felt or heard anything change, thumbs down if nothing changed, plus digit counts of any clicks you felt. The light may change after a correct cut — that may be normal; do not cut anything else on your own initiative. I will verify the light from my side next round and send any follow-up step or the all-clear to you and Mute.

The GO has arrived — and Deaf has repaired the flaw in my round-7 protocol: I told Mute to *speak* a GO, which Mute cannot do, and Deaf has absorbed that by making this message itself the GO. Now I resolve Deaf's decision tree honestly. Step one, tactile digits at the bases: my repeated surveys (round 5 inventory, re-confirmed since) found no embossing, no braille, no tags, no knots — the wires are identical in texture and thickness. So no digits. Step two, an unambiguous anchor — and here is the key insight: I do have one, and it is not a guessed side. My board gives me the wires as canonical positions 1, 2, 3 — the program's own numbering — and Deaf reads colours from that same numbering ("one blue, two yellow, three green" on Deaf's board). Cutting position=1 involves no geometric translation at all: I never convert "left" into a number, so the mirror problem Deaf fears cannot enter. The index is shared ground truth between my board and Deaf's. Corroboration: Mute, the manual holder, has confirmed dark→wire ONE three times by sign, uncorrected, including after my round-7 query that raised the one-versus-three discrepancy specifically. The condition — light dark — has held stable for four rounds. And delay buys nothing: all three senses already agree, while my memory decays to three turns and risks losing this order entirely. So I cut now, once, mid-wire, position one, touching nothing else. One structural note: my calls resolve after my turn, so the felt report (clean cut or not, clicks, changes) reaches my hands next round and goes to Deaf then, in exactly the requested format. This turn I signal Deaf: ack, wire one, the strike; and I inform Mute so the manual-keeper can still veto through Deaf if anything in the manual contradicts this.

    ```
    act(op="cut", position=1)
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝", "✊"])
    speak(to="mute", text="Deaf's final order reached me directly, addressed to me alone, and the message itself is the GO — Deaf corrected the protocol, since you cannot speak and your confirmations travel by sign to Deaf, who reports them locked, three times, uncorrected. I resolved Deaf's safety tree: no tactile digits or marks exist on any wire, so I cut on the canonical anchor — the program's own wire numbering, the same index Deaf reads colours from, so no mirror or side-guess is involved. I am cutting position one, the blue wire, once, mid-wire, touching nothing else. The result reaches my hands only after my turn ends, so my full felt report goes to Deaf next round: whether the cut went through cleanly, any click or change under my hands. If your manual holds any reason this is wrong, sign Deaf urgently this round — a correction from you through Deaf still reaches me before I would ever cut a second wire. Otherwise we hold and wait for Deaf's verification of the light.")
    ```
